A warm welcome to Tunstall Primary School
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website and learn more about our wonderful school community. As a voluntary aided, two-form entry Church of England primary school set in the beautiful East Kent countryside, we are proud to be a nurturing, inclusive and ambitious school where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive.At the heart of everything we do is our vision:
We believe that God’s abundance is for everyone… “A place where everyone can flourish.” (John 10:10)

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast & After School Club -  Tunstall C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Our fantastic Breakfast Club runs every weekday morning.
Breakfast club is managed by a team Miss Kennett (Breakfast Club Lead), Mrs H Burlton, Mrs Mannering, Mrs S Hewett and Mrs C Elliott. We provide activities to engage all year groups, including, outdoor activities (weather permitting), workout Wednesdays, and craft Fridays. All of our activities are current topic based and we have seasonal end of term celebrations.
Pre booking is required, however, there are now two payment tiers/options for Breakfast Club; -
Please book via the Arbor App – no cash transactions.
You will need to ensure you have a balance on your account to enable payments to be taken, the same way, as those who pay for a school dinner. Each day a register will be taken for each pupil in attendance and your account will be debited accordingly. If you need to use both options at any time you will need to have credit on both the options.
Voucher payments are still acceptable, please ensure that you purchase these in advance, to avoid a debt accumulating, then email them to the School Office so that the credit can be manually entered onto the Breakfast Club account by School staff. Each time the club is attended the amount will be deducted in the same way as non-voucher payments.
We have an email specifically for Breakfast Club and any queries you may have please drop an email to breakfastclub@tunstall.kent.sch.uk
After-School Club
Mrs Oxlee, the After School Club Manager, runs the club with Mrs Elliott, providing activities to engage all year groups, some of which will cover homework tasks. Our experienced HLTA, Mrs Frith, provides reading and phonics support daily for all children attending.
The sessions run from 3.30 pm to 6 pm, Monday to Friday and must be booked in advance with at least 24 hours’ notice. Bookings can be made via the Arbor App.
If you wish to book on the day (subject to availability), you must do so by 10am so that we can ensure we have enough staff and food can be prepared by our kitchen staff before service ends.
We are able to cater for dietary requirements as long as we are advised of specific requirements in advance.
Registration FormAfter School Club information
For more information please contact the school office, or speak to one of the After School Club staff.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music & Drama at Tunstall School -  Tunstall C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music and drama are central to life at Tunstall — vital, joyful and powerful vehicles for developing the whole child.
Our curriculum uses the Discovery approach to give every child frequent, purposeful opportunities to sing, play, compose and perform. Learning music develops physical coordination, listening, pattern recognition and the mathematical skills needed to keep a steady pulse; these skills are deliberately taught and linked to wider learning so that musical progress supports reading, maths, oracy and creative thinking. Drama complements this by building confidence, empathy and expressive language: children learn to inhabit character, structure a story, present to an audience and collaborate with others in imaginative, risk-taking ways.
We are ambitious: through our Music Plus programme every child will learn to play a musical instrument (in addition to voice) before leaving Tunstall, and all KS2 children are offered further peripatetic lessons across a range of instruments. Music and drama are woven into Discovery topics, enriched by peripatetic teaching, after-school clubs, ensemble rehearsals, community partnerships and cross-school performances. Assessment focuses on progression in technique, creativity and performance confidence rather than single outputs; children plan, rehearse, reflect and refine — moving from imitation to composition and independent performance. The result is a vibrant, inclusive arts offer that nurtures resilience, cultural curiosity and the practical, transferable skills pupils need to flourish now and in the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths -  Tunstall C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Maths at Tunstall CofE Primary is practical, playful and purposeful. From EYFS to Year 2 children learn through hands-on experiences using manipulatives — ten frames, counters, number lines and fingers — which help them build secure number sense.
Pupils are encouraged to find their own ways of recording ideas, from drawings and dot patterns to formal number sentences. Most lessons follow the White Rose scheme and, from Year 1, children take part in a daily “Fluent in Five” session to build rapid recall and confidence. Our early-phase focus is on three core strands: Number, Operations (adding, subtracting, multiplying, dividing) and Geometry & Spatial Reasoning.
In Key Stage 2 we deepen those foundations so children become fluent, resilient mathematicians ready for secondary school. Lessons combine fluency, reasoning and problem-solving: pupils practise mental and written methods regularly, explain and justify their thinking using precise mathematical vocabulary and tackle problems in real-life and cross-curricular contexts. Classrooms from Years 3–6 promote active participation with concrete resources, visual representations and collaborative tasks; teachers use spaced practice and retrieval to secure long-term learning. We expect fluent recall of multiplication and related division facts by the end of Year 4, supported through low-stakes quizzes and Times Tables Rock Stars. By the end of Year 6 pupils are confident, independent problem-solvers who can apply efficient strategies and reason mathematically across a wide range of contexts.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages -  Tunstall C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
At Tunstall, all children in KS2 learn French on a regular basis. We aim for our children to be confident and resilient global citizens who build on cultural capital.
As much as possible, the lessons are taught in the target language so that children can develop the skills to communicate confidently when in French-speaking countries. They are encouraged to talk in French every lesson. The learning of languages at KS2 has been statutory since 2014.
There are many benefits to learning a language:
These are skills which children can transfer to other subjects and their own lives.
At Tunstall we use and adapt The Language Angels scheme which is supplemented by songs from La Jolie Ronde. We also play many games to practise new vocabulary. Children are taught translation strategies, pronunciation, intonation and awareness of genders and adjectival agreement. Not only this, children learn about the culture and geography of countries around the world. By the end of Year 6, children working at the expected level will be able to write a paragraph about themselves, which is mostly accurate. They will also be able to role-play short conversations in different contexts.
This is unique to language learning.

Medication at school

Please note, if your child has Asthma or requires an epi pen or they have an ongoing medical condition, please contact Miss Hill, Deputy Head and Inclusion deputyhead@tunstall.kent.sch.uk
How to notify us if your child is unwell
If your child is unwell and unable to attend school, please email flo@tunstall.kent.sch.uk before the start of the school day each day they are absent. If your child has sickness or diarrhoea, they can return to school 48 hours after the symptoms have stopped.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tiny & Little Lights -  Tunstall C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Tunstall C of E Primary School is excited to invite you to our parent and child groups for the local community.
These fun, teacher led sessions will introduce early phonics through songs, nursery rhymes, games and activities, encouraging a love of reading from a very early age.
Tiny Lights of Tunstall
Tiny Lights of Tunstall is open to parents/carers and babies from 4-6months to approximately 24 months and will gently introduce you to activities you can do with your baby to support their early language acquisition. We will use well known nursery rhymes with actions and props to help your child learn to recognise sounds around them and make purposeful noises themselves. We will also share simple yet fun books and model how to make this an exciting and beneficial activity at home. We are a Makaton friendly school, so simple Makaton signs are also introduced.
Little Lights of Tunstall
Little Lights of Tunstall offers a slightly more energetic session for those with confident walkers and explorers, aged 2 years up to preschool. We continue to look at sounds and speech through nursery rhymes, songs, books and activities to support and prepare them for learning to read and write when they enter Reception. Above all, we want them to foster a love of books and a craving to understand the print on the page.
Each class is capped at 15 families (typically 1 baby/child and 1 parent/carer, but other family members are very welcome) and spaces are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, with a waiting list where necessary. To register your interest, please follow the link at the top of the page. A six week block is £18.
Sessions last 45 minutes and take place in the Small hall at the school. There is limited space for buggies/car seats so please only bring them indoors if necessary. We ask that you remove your shoes when you come in and wear socks.
The class themes will change each week, all year round, but the skills and knowledge progression will be repeated. Children learn best through repetition… in a fun environment of course.

pageCache.pageTitle: Uniform -  Tunstall C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
When children are in school, they are part of a community and by wearing a simple school uniform we hope to promote a feeling of equality, partnership and belonging.
At our school, uniform is an important part of belonging to our community. Wearing a simple, consistent uniform helps promote equality, partnership, and pride in our shared identity.
All children are required to wear school uniform, with every item clearly marked with their name. Parents may choose items with our school logo, but plain alternatives are equally welcome.
We have two types of uniform:
In EYFS/Red Class, children wear sports kit every day, with an optional coloured T-shirt change on their PE/Forest School day.From Year 1 onwards, children wear their sports kit on two days each week and their formal uniform on three days.
